To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the entanglements of the excited states in CFTs are always larger than those of the vacuum and the quantum dimension can be identified as the increase of the entanglement.

the quantum dimension of a primary operator in a two-dimensional CFT can be computed from the entanglement growth of an excited state obtained by acting with that operator on the vacuum, and that this holds for any excited state in any rational CFT.

1) the entanglement growth in excited states of 2d CFT is universal, i.e., the same as in the ground states; 2) in rational CFTs, the entanglement grows by a finite amount that is given by the log of the primary operator’s quantum dimension.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: what is the relation between the quantum dimension of primary operators in rational CFTs and the increase of the entanglement under its time evolution?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the quantum dimension of a primary operator coincides with the increase of entanglement entropy under its time evolution, which is a generalization of the well-known statement that the vacuum quantum dimension coincides with the entropy of entanglement.
in two dimensional conformally invariant theories the entanglement of a subregion is determined by the quantum dimension of a primary field inserted on it.
the log of the conformal dimension of a primary operator is the quantum dimension of that primary operator.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quantum dimension can be understood as the increase of entanglement entropy under its time evolution.
the quantum dimension of a primary operator is the minimal increase of the entanglement under the time evolution of the excited states created by it.
the quantum dimension is a universal constant that characterizes how fast the entanglement of an excited state increases in two-dimensional CFTs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quantum dimension of a CFT primary is a universal quantity, which is independent of the CFT and the choice of the vacuum.
, in CFTs, the quantum dimension of an operator can be interpreted as the increase of entanglement entropy when the operator is inserted.
in CFTs the quantum dimension of a primary operator is the same as the increase of the entanglement in the system after acting on the vacuum with the primary operator.
